audit_findings.title: Current share count is paired with a pre-leverage earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased by $2.527 billion from September 30, 2025 to June 30, 2026; quarterly net interest expense increased by $26.978 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: The July 2026 share denominator reflects debt-funded repurchases, while the $596.2 million OE anchor predates most of the resulting interest burden; future common-equity OE is therefore overstated unless updated for the June 2026 capital structure.
audit_findings.evidence: Total debt balance was $3.1 billion as of September 30, 2025, compared with $2.2 billion as of September 30, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch, not merely a possible risk. Shares fell from 23.764 million at September 30, 2025 to 21.597 million at June 30, 2026 while debt rose from $3.056 billion to $5.582 billion. The filed $27.0 million year-over-year quarterly increase in net interest expense is large relative to the $596.2 million anchor and is reasonably capable of materially lowering all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Build a post-FY2025 borrowing-and-repurchase schedule, calculate normalized after-tax interest on the June 30, 2026 debt structure, replace the anchor or first forecast year with common-equity OE carrying that burden, and rerun all scenarios using the same fully diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: Accrual revenue may overstate cash owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $100.377 million FY2025 accounts-receivable use of cash, equal to 16.8% of the $596.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Point-in-time license revenue raises net income before corresponding customer billing or collection; if required working-capital investment was omitted from OE, the historical series and trend anchor are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Furthermore, this point-in-time revenue recognition can create a significant difference between the timing of our revenue recognition and the actual customer billing under the contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The recognition-versus-billing mismatch and the $100.377 million FY2025 accounts-receivable cash outflow are demonstrated. Whether the OE construction already captured or normalized that outflow is unresolved. Its scale is material relative to the anchor, so the issue is reasonably capable of changing the valuation rather than being only a monitoring item.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the large FY2025 renewal to recognized revenue, billed and unbilled receivables, cash collected through June 2026, and the exact working-capital adjustment used in each OE year; rerun the trend and scenarios if the required investment was omitted.

audit_findings.title: Mortgage-score growth faces an identified regime change
audit_findings.mechanism: Lender choice among score models or use of fewer bureau scores could reduce mortgage-score volumes, constrain pricing, and invalidate the 7% and 9% growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: Other changes implemented by FHFA, Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac could also affect the demand for FICO Scores and thus could have similar adverse effects on our business, including, for example, the change announced by the FHFA Director in July 2025 permitting mortgage originators to choose the credit score they submit with mortgages delivered to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac or a potential future change permitting mortgage originators to underwrite loans using credit scores from fewer than three national consumer reporting agencies.
audit_findings.explanation: The regulatory change and competitive exposure are identified, but the supplied filings do not demonstrate a present earnings impairment. Through June 2026, Scores revenue instead increased 45% year over year for the nine-month period, primarily from mortgage pricing and volume. The downside remains forward-looking and cannot be quantified from the record.
audit_findings.action: Monitor implementation dates, lender adoption, FICO versus competing-model share, scores ordered per mortgage, realized unit pricing, bureau pass-through behavior, and post-change volumes; rerun growth scenarios when observed adoption or pricing data establish an effect.

audit_findings.title: Antitrust litigation could impose an unmodeled common-equity cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Damages or settlement would be a direct equity claim; pricing restrictions or an injunction would reduce future Scores OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The court dismissed with prejudice all claims in the lawsuit other than a Sherman Act Section 2 claim and accompanying state law claims against FICO, which were allowed to proceed through the discovery stage of the litigation.
audit_findings.explanation: The surviving Sherman Act and state-law claims are demonstrated and remain in discovery, but the record supplies no damages estimate, requested-remedy valuation, insurance recovery, or probability-weighted loss. The June 2026 filing states that reasonably possible legal losses were not materially exposed individually or in aggregate, yet that accounting assessment does not resolve the valuation effect of possible injunctive or pricing remedies. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current docket, operative complaint, claimed damages period, requested injunctions, discovery and dispositive-motion developments, insurance terms, and any accrual or settlement analysis; separately rerun the bridge for a quantified cash claim and OE scenarios for any pricing or distribution remedy.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may retain a non-durable tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.638 million reported benefit; full removal from 2025 OE would reduce the log-trend anchor by approximately $9.5 million, or 1.6%
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-recurring excess SBC tax benefit raises FY2025 net income and cash-tax-based OE; normalization affects the historical OE observation and therefore the fitted anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in our effective tax rate in fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024 was due to an increase in excess tax benefits related to share-based compensation.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in OE is unresolved, but scale can be bounded. Even assuming the entire $27.638 million benefit is removed dollar-for-dollar from 2025 OE, the ten-year log-trend anchor falls only from $596.2 million to approximately $586.7 million because the adjustment is smoothed across the regression. That roughly 1.6% anchor effect is too small to change the conclusion when the $932.26 market price exceeds even the $538.74 bull value by $393.52 per share.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the cash-tax treatment of excess SBC benefits in every OE year and, if retained, rerun the log trend using normalized cash taxes; no separate terminal adjustment is needed unless the historical review finds materially larger recurring distortions.
